sub.text: Rock Hunter is a game. Here is what Spirit and Opportunity really found on Mars.

slides.title: TWO ROVERS, TWO SITES
slides.text: The twins landed on opposite sides of Mars in January 2004. Spirit landed at Gusev Crater, a possible former lake in a giant impact crater. Opportunity landed at Meridiani Planum, where mineral deposits suggested that Mars had a wet history.
slides.why: Both landing sites were chosen because they might hold clues of past water.
slides.mentor: Here is what the real rovers found. One clue at a time!

slides.title: BLUEBERRIES IN EAGLE CRATER
slides.text: Opportunity landed inside a small crater and scored a "hole in one": small spherical deposits of hematite, a mineral that typically forms in water. They were nicknamed the "blueberries".
slides.why: Studying them during the three-month prime mission provided evidence of a watery ancient environment.

slides.title: RIPPLES AND SALTS
slides.text: The same rocks showed cross-bedding (layers in curved patterns) and sulfate salts, including jarosite, a mineral that forms in acidic water.
slides.why: Water was there, but acidic water made conditions harder for life to thrive.

slides.title: SPIRIT'S SURPRISE
slides.text: At a place called Comanche, Spirit found rocks rich in carbonates that formed with near-neutral water. Later, while dragging a stuck wheel, it churned up soil that was 90% pure silica at "Home Plate".
slides.why: On Earth, silica like that usually forms in hot springs or hot steam vents: places where water and heat meet.

slides.title: LONGER THAN PLANNED
slides.text: Both rovers were designed for 90 sols (about three Earth months). Spirit worked until 2010 and drove 7.7 km. Opportunity drove 45.16 km and last communicated on June 10, 2018, as a planet-wide dust storm covered its location.
slides.why: Every extra year meant new places, new rocks and more clues.

slides.title: THE BIG PICTURE
slides.text: By studying the rock record, Spirit and Opportunity confirmed that water was long-standing on the surface of Mars in ancient times. Some places, like Comanche and Endeavour Crater's clays, once had friendlier conditions for tiny microbes.
slides.why: The rovers were not built to look for life, but they showed where to look next.

real.title: WHAT IT MEANS
real.text: Later missions like Curiosity and Perseverance went to Mars to look for places that could once have supported life.

slides.mentor: Answer one question, then it's time to send your results home!
